implemented.label: Separate teams
implemented.statement: A new player can create an independent force and distant starting area, or request an owner-approved join to an existing team.
implemented.portal_phrase: Create a separate team and distant starting area, or request an owner-approved join to a friend.

implemented.label: Team evolution
implemented.statement: Each team has a paired enemy force and an independent raw evolution ledger on every recorded surface; connected time, that team's worm/spawner kills, and new pollution consumed by unit spawners on that surface feed it.
implemented.portal_phrase: Enemy evolution is tracked per team and per surface from connected time, own worm/spawner kills, and new pollution consumed by nests on that surface.

implemented.label: Nests hostile to everyone
implemented.statement: Every team's paired enemy force is hostile to every registered human team, its own and all others alike, so no team can shelter behind another team's nests; paired enemy forces stay friendly with each other and with the vanilla enemy force, and human-team diplomacy is never written by the mod.
implemented.portal_phrase: Every team's nests treat every player as an enemy, so no base is safe inside a rival team's nest field, while the nests themselves never fight each other.

evidence.contains: paired enemy is not hostile to the other human team

implemented.label: Space Age planets
implemented.statement: After a team's first physical arrival, one stable separated spawn is generated asynchronously on each real planet while native terrain and progression stay intact; on Vulcanus, the Oarc workaround grants a spawn territory by destroying a tracked demolisher only if it enters the fixed six-chunk warning radius.
implemented.portal_phrase: With Space Age enabled, each team receives one stable separated spawn after physically reaching a new planet; platforms and remote view are excluded. On Vulcanus, the Oarc workaround removes a tracked demolisher only if it enters the six-chunk warning radius around a team spawn.

implemented.label: Electricity isolation
implemented.statement: Direct cross-team copper links are removed, conflicting player/robot placements are rejected and refunded, script-raised conflicts fail closed after their creator resumes, and sharing requires mutual team-owner opt-in.
implemented.portal_phrase: Electric networks are isolated by default; deliberate sharing requires both team owners to opt in.

implemented.label: Immediate offline preservation
implemented.statement: When the last human leaves a team, tracked team-owned entities immediately become unbreakable; the first teammate back restores each exact prior destructible state.
implemented.portal_phrase: Offline protection activates immediately when the last human leaves a team: tracked team-owned entities become unbreakable, then the first teammate back restores each exact prior destructible state.

implemented.label: Shared radar discovery
implemented.statement: Every 10 seconds, already-generated chunks around connected team characters and team-owned radars are shared with every registered human team without merging forces, economies, evolution, or electric networks.
implemented.portal_phrase: Connected players and team radars share their nearby, already-generated map discovery with every registered human team, without merging forces, economies, evolution, or electric networks.

implemented.label: Robot policy
implemented.statement: Per-team logistic and construction caps aggregate every fixed network and surface; policy can be disabled, warning-only, or enforced by pausing only registered crafting machines whose current recipe produces a capped robot class, while preserving each machine's prior script-disabled state.
implemented.portal_phrase: Configurable per-team robot limits aggregate all fixed networks and surfaces; enforcement pauses only crafting machines currently producing the capped robot class, and never moves, deletes, or hides robot items.

implemented.label: Optional AI Assistance
implemented.statement: AI Assistance is off by default and ships as one automation-science technology, a powered Uplink, a one-time pairing code a player creates there as their own explicit opt-in, revocation, and exactly 29 scope-checked MCP tools.
implemented.portal_phrase: Optional AI Assistance is off by default and uses one automation-science technology, a powered Uplink, one-time pairing codes a player creates as their own explicit opt-in, and 29 scoped MCP tools.

limitations.label: Surface-global nest consumption
limitations.statement: Factorio exposes cumulative pollution output statistics per surface rather than per force. Sceatorio sums only keys whose runtime entity prototype is a unit spawner, so every recorded team receives the same newly consumed delta; no proximity or triangulation is used. Trees and scrubbers can reduce future evolution by intercepting pollution before nests, while evolution already credited never decreases.
limitations.portal_phrase: Pollution evolution follows surface-global nest consumption rather than gross factory emissions

limitations.label: Fresh 2.0 worlds for offline protection
limitations.statement: Normal save/load is supported, but offline entity registration is event-driven for fresh 2.0 worlds; installing it onto an existing untracked world has no retrofit guarantee.
limitations.portal_phrase: Normal save/load is supported, but offline entity registration targets fresh 2.0 worlds; installing it onto an existing untracked world has no retrofit guarantee.

limitations.label: Unannounced third-party entities
limitations.statement: Script-raised builds and clones are checked after their creator resumes, and a bounded next-tick audit catches silent companion poles around every visible electric build. Factorio exposes no general creation event for unrelated entities silently created later by another mod, so exact third-party releases remain an operator-audited trust boundary.
limitations.portal_phrase: A bounded next-tick audit catches silent companion poles around visible electric builds; unrelated entities created without any Factorio lifecycle event remain a trusted-mod boundary.

limitations.label: Previously accepted implicit power
limitations.statement: Revoking mutual intent makes direct cross-team copper unauthorized and prevents new player/robot implicit overlaps, but an implicit overlap accepted while sharing was active has no direct wire or exact delayed refund and must be relocated manually.
limitations.portal_phrase: Revoking mutual power sharing immediately makes direct cross-team copper unauthorized and prevents new player/robot implicit overlaps, but an implicit overlap accepted while sharing was active must be relocated manually.

limitations.label: AI control and transport boundary
limitations.statement: No MCP tool moves, mines, crafts, fights, teleports, places entities, runs arbitrary Lua/RCON, or changes generic factory state; the local path requires loopback Lua UDP, one pairing code crosses it once, and bearer credentials never enter UDP or the save.
limitations.portal_phrase: No MCP tool controls the character or places entities, and bearer credentials never enter Factorio UDP or the save; the local bridge requires Factorio's loopback Lua UDP flag.

limitations.label: No public AI endpoint
limitations.statement: The tested release path is a local stdio MCP sidecar over loopback UDP; an internet-facing Streamable HTTP/OAuth deployment is intentionally not shipped by this repository.
limitations.portal_phrase: The tested AI path is local stdio over loopback UDP; this mod does not expose a public AI or Factorio endpoint.

limitations.label: Exact Factorio target
limitations.statement: The 2.x release line targets the Factorio 2.1.12 runtime and API rather than the older 1.1 Mod Portal line.
